clues.text: A Jew from Alexandria, an eloquent man well versed in the Scriptures, arrived in Ephesus.
This fervent preacher taught accurately about Jesus, though he knew only the baptism of John.
When he spoke boldly in the synagogue at Ephesus, Priscilla and Aquila took him aside and taught him more accurately.
When he set out for Achaia, the brothers wrote to the disciples there asking them to welcome him.
Believers in Corinth quarreled, some saying 'I follow Paul' while others claimed to follow this man.
Paul wrote to Corinth that he planted the seed, this man watered it, but God made it grow.
Paul told Titus to equip this man and Zenas the lawyer so they would have everything they needed.
